packageText:
TITLE: Hemorrhagic Ovarian Cyst

SOURCE STATUS
- [Both] This fused master source combines RadPrimer Hemorrhagic Cyst with STATdx Hemorrhagic Ovarian Cyst.
- [RadPrimer] Canonical hierarchy: All Categories > Basic > Ultrasound > Female Pelvis Basic > Hemorrhagic Cyst
- [RadPrimer] Canonical deck path: Corebook::Ultrasound::Female Pelvis Basic::Hemorrhagic Cyst::Hemorrhagic Ovarian Cyst
- [Both] Core Radiology evidence was requested but not supplied in this browser bundle; do not label later output as Core-supported unless a later run provides auditable Core text.

MASTER SUMMARY
- [Both] A hemorrhagic ovarian cyst is a physiologic ovarian cyst, most often a corpus luteum cyst, with internal hemorrhage. Hemorrhage may also occur into a follicular cyst, and acute hemorrhage can occasionally occur into an established endometrioma.
- [Both] The central recognition pattern is an intraovarian or exophytic ovarian cyst with avascular internal blood products: fine lace-like or reticular fibrin strands, fishnet/cobweb echoes, retracting clot, clot fragments with angular or concave margins, or a fluid-fluid/debris level.
- [Both] Color Doppler should show no vascularity within clot or fibrin strands. Peripheral wall or corpus luteum flow can be prominent and can create a ring-of-fire appearance.
- [Both] Most hemorrhagic ovarian cysts resolve or substantially decrease within about 6-8 weeks, and most leave no sequela. Larger cysts are more likely to cause acute pain, rupture, hemoperitoneum, or serve as a lead point for torsion.

ULTRASOUND RECOGNITION
- [Both] Endovaginal ultrasound with color Doppler is the best imaging test. Confirm ovarian origin by identifying surrounding ovarian tissue, a claw sign, or motion with the ovary rather than separation from the ovary under gentle probe pressure.
- [RadPrimer] RadPrimer image 1 shows the canonical grayscale lace-like internal echoes and posterior acoustic enhancement of a complex right ovarian hemorrhagic cyst.
- [RadPrimer] RadPrimer image 2 adds the Doppler rule: the cyst contents are avascular while displaced peripheral ovarian parenchyma shows flow and a venous waveform.
- [STATdx] STATdx emphasizes four common grayscale patterns: diffuse echogenicity that can resemble dermoid, reticular fibrin strands, retracting avascular clot with convex/concave/straight margins, and a simple-appearing cyst with a fluid-fluid level.
- [Both] Posterior acoustic enhancement or through transmission helps confirm a cystic lesion when blood products make it look solid. Internal Doppler vascularity or papillary projections argue against uncomplicated hemorrhagic cyst.
- [Both] Rupture may cause echogenic or variably echogenic pelvic free fluid. If fluid is substantial, scan the upper abdomen, including the right kidney/Morrison pouch region and subphrenic spaces, to assess hemoperitoneum extent.
- [RadPrimer] RadPrimer image 3 shows complex cul-de-sac fluid from rupture, and RadPrimer image 7 shows extension of fluid to the hepatorenal fossa.

CT AND MR
- [Both] CT may show an adnexal cyst with high-attenuation blood products, a fluid-fluid level, peripheral enhancement, and hemoperitoneum. CT is often obtained first in acute pelvic pain, but ultrasound better defines internal cyst architecture.
- [STATdx] The CT sentinel clot sign can help localize the ovarian bleeding source: fluid around the ovary is higher attenuation than fluid farther away. STATdx images 21 and 22 show ruptured cyst CT examples, including a wall defect in one case.
- [RadPrimer] RadPrimer images 8 and 9 show large-volume CT hemoperitoneum; RadPrimer image 9 also shows active bleeding in the right adnexal region on coronal CT.
- [Both] MR blood-product signal is variable. Classic teaching is T1 and T2 hyperintensity, but STATdx stresses that signal depends on blood age, hematocrit, protein concentration, hemoglobin form, and clot formation or retraction.
- [Both] T1 fat-suppressed imaging is useful because persistent high signal after fat suppression supports blood products rather than fat-containing dermoid. RadPrimer image 10 is the canonical selected T1 fat-suppressed example; STATdx image 18 is kept as the T2 companion image.

DIFFERENTIAL AND PITFALLS
- [Both] Endometrioma is a major mimic. It more often has uniform low-level or ground-glass echoes, wall echogenic foci, chronic cyclic pain/infertility, and little change on follow-up; a hemorrhagic cyst should resolve or shrink. Acute hemorrhage into an endometrioma can overlap, with follow-up showing clot resolution but persistent background endometrioma.
- [Both] Solid ovarian mass or ovarian cancer is suggested by papillary projections, mural nodules, thick septa, absence of cystic through-transmission, and internal vascularity. Angular avascular clot fragments can simulate solid tissue but should not enhance or vascularize internally.
- [Both] Ectopic pregnancy remains a critical mimic when ring-of-fire flow is seen. A corpus luteum or hemorrhagic corpus luteum is intraovarian and moves with the ovary; a tubal ectopic is typically extraovarian and may separate from the ovary with probe pressure.
- [STATdx] Dermoid cyst can mimic a reticular pattern through hair mesh, but other signs such as Rokitansky nodule, calcification, or fat-fluid level should be present.
- [Both] Torsion may coexist with or complicate a hemorrhagic cyst. Look for enlarged tender ovary, peripheral follicles, parenchymal inhomogeneity, abnormal position, twisted pedicle, and abnormal venous/arterial flow; normal flow does not fully exclude torsion.
- [Both] Pelvic abscess or tuboovarian abscess is favored by fever, leukocytosis, marked tenderness, inflammatory loss of tissue planes, pyosalpinx, purulent discharge, and possible perihepatic inflammatory change.

PATHOLOGY AND CLINICAL COURSE
- [Both] Most hemorrhagic ovarian cysts result from bleeding into a functional follicular or corpus luteum cyst, commonly at ovulation. Grossly, the cyst may be thin or thick walled and contain clot or serosanguineous fluid.
- [Both] Presentation ranges from incidental finding to acute pelvic pain. Severe pain often improves within hours, and most masses disappear within about 8 weeks.
- [RadPrimer] Hemorrhagic cysts may complicate ovulation induction or assisted reproduction and can be confused clinically with torsion or ovarian hyperstimulation. Fetal ovarian cysts may hemorrhage or torse, with an in-utero fluid-fluid level being suspicious.
- [STATdx] Late postmenopausal patients should not ovulate; a hemorrhagic-appearing cystic lesion in that setting should prompt concern for malignancy rather than routine physiologic-cyst follow-up.

MANAGEMENT ORIENTATION
- [Both] SRU-style management for classic hemorrhagic cysts in reproductive-age patients: 5 cm or smaller needs no follow-up; larger than 5 cm gets short-interval ultrasound follow-up in about 6-12 weeks, ideally during the follicular phase when feasible.
- [Both] Early postmenopausal hemorrhagic-appearing cysts should get follow-up ultrasound to document resolution. Late postmenopausal hemorrhagic-appearing cysts should be considered for surgical evaluation.
- [Both] Rupture with hemoperitoneum usually receives supportive management if the patient is hemodynamically stable. Surgery is reserved for hemodynamic instability, significant intraperitoneal hemorrhage, torsion, or severe persistent symptoms.
- [RadPrimer] Recurrent hemorrhagic cysts may be managed with ovulation suppression.

IMAGE CURATION SUMMARY
- [Both] Actual image_evidence files were inspected with all-image and candidate-pair contact sheets before duplicate classification.
- [Both] STATdx does not fully cover the RadPrimer image set. Only RadPrimer image 10 has an exact STATdx duplicate.
- [RadPrimer] RadPrimer images 1-10 remain selected primary images because RadPrimer is the canonical hierarchy/backbone and the images include unique teaching points not fully replaced by STATdx.
- [STATdx] STATdx image 17 is archived as an optional exact duplicate of RadPrimer image 10. STATdx image 18 remains selected as the T2 MR companion, so the MR cluster is preserved.
- [STATdx] All other STATdx images remain selected primary images as distinct examples, modality variants, same-patient companion images, or recognition reinforcement.

PRIMARY IMAGE APPENDIX
- RadPrimer image 1: Grayscale endovaginal ultrasound of a complex right ovarian cyst with lace-like fibrin strands and posterior enhancement. Teaching role: canonical reticular hemorrhagic cyst.
- RadPrimer image 2: Doppler ultrasound of an avascular hemorrhagic cyst with peripheral ovarian parenchymal flow and venous waveform. Teaching role: avascular clot and ovarian-origin confirmation.
- RadPrimer image 3: Transvaginal ultrasound showing complex pelvic fluid in the cul-de-sac from ruptured hemorrhagic cyst. Teaching role: pelvic hemoperitoneum.
- RadPrimer image 4: Laparoscopy photograph showing blood in the cul-de-sac and clot on the ovarian capsule. Teaching role: surgical rupture correlation.
- RadPrimer image 5: Color Doppler hemorrhagic corpus luteum with peripheral flow. Teaching role: ring-of-fire pitfall versus ectopic pregnancy.
- RadPrimer image 6: Transabdominal ultrasound showing enlarged kissing ovaries with cysts containing echoes. Teaching role: bilateral/ovulation-context variant.
- RadPrimer image 7: Upper abdominal ultrasound showing hepatorenal fossa fluid. Teaching role: scanning for large hemoperitoneum.
- RadPrimer image 8: Axial contrast CT showing high-attenuation upper-abdominal hemoperitoneum. Teaching role: CT hemoperitoneum extension.
- RadPrimer image 9: Coronal contrast CT showing large hemoperitoneum and active right adnexal bleeding. Teaching role: severe rupture with active bleeding.
- RadPrimer image 10: Axial T1 fat-suppressed MR showing persistent high-signal blood products. Teaching role: canonical MR blood-product/fat-exclusion example.
- STATdx image 1: Doppler ultrasound showing diffusely echogenic hemorrhagic cyst mimicking dermoid, with follow-up resolution. Teaching role: echogenic-pattern pitfall.
- STATdx image 2: Doppler ultrasound showing avascular reticular fibrin strands. Teaching role: lace-like/fishnet recognition reinforcement.
- STATdx image 3: Doppler ultrasound showing fine reticular meshwork and straight-edge retracting clot. Teaching role: retracting clot.
- STATdx image 4: Doppler ultrasound of hemorrhagic cyst with retracted avascular clot. Teaching role: avascular clot recognition.
- STATdx image 5: Doppler ultrasound showing fishnet appearance. Teaching role: classic hemorrhagic cyst pattern.
- STATdx image 6: Doppler ultrasound of hemorrhagic corpus luteal cyst in pregnancy with ring-of-fire vascularity. Teaching role: ectopic pregnancy pitfall.
- STATdx image 7: Axial T1 MR showing intermediate to slightly high signal right ovarian cystic mass. Teaching role: MR signal variant.
- STATdx image 8: Axial T1 fat-suppressed MR from the same patient showing increased lesion conspicuity and fat exclusion. Teaching role: same-patient MR cluster.
- STATdx image 9: Axial T2 MR from the same patient showing persistent high signal. Teaching role: T2 signal variability.
- STATdx image 10: Transvaginal ultrasound from the same patient showing low-level reticular echoes and posterior enhancement. Teaching role: MR/US correlation.
- STATdx image 11: Doppler ultrasound showing fishnet fibrin strands plus retracting clot. Teaching role: combined reticular/clot pattern.
- STATdx image 12: Transvaginal ultrasound showing fibrinous strands and retracting clot. Teaching role: alternate same-disease example.
- STATdx image 13: Axial T1 MR showing hypointense cyst with posterior hyperintense fluid-fluid level. Teaching role: variable T1 signal and small-volume hemorrhage.
- STATdx image 14: Contrast-enhanced T1 MR from the same patient showing thin wall enhancement without internal enhancement. Teaching role: no enhancing solid component.
- STATdx image 15: Axial T2 MR from the same patient showing clot separated from serous component. Teaching role: T2 fluid-fluid level.
- STATdx image 16: Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound from the same patient showing a smooth retracting clot edge. Teaching role: US correlation for MR fluid-fluid case.
- STATdx image 18: Axial T2 MR companion image showing low-signal clot, with follow-up near-complete involution by 6 weeks. Teaching role: T2 clot and resolution context.
- STATdx image 19: Doppler ultrasound in acute pain showing avascular adnexal hemorrhagic cyst and pelvic blood. Teaching role: ruptured HOC with pelvic clot.
- STATdx image 20: Transvaginal Doppler ultrasound from the same patient showing hemoperitoneum around the uterus and cul-de-sac. Teaching role: pelvic hemoperitoneum cluster.
- STATdx image 21: Axial contrast CT showing ruptured collapsed right hemorrhagic cyst with high-attenuation fluid and sentinel clot sign. Teaching role: CT localization of bleeding.
- STATdx image 22: Axial contrast CT showing ruptured left hemorrhagic cyst with wall defect and high-attenuation fluid. Teaching role: CT wall-defect rupture sign.
- STATdx image 23: Sagittal transvaginal ultrasound showing hypoechoic hemorrhagic cyst with low-level linear fishnet echoes. Teaching role: alternate fishnet example.
- STATdx image 24: Sagittal endovaginal ultrasound showing a straight margin of retracting clot. Teaching role: retracting clot sign.

ARCHIVED DUPLICATE IMAGE NOTES
- STATdx image 17 is an exact duplicate of RadPrimer image 10 by direct visual inspection of the staged image_evidence files. Archive STATdx image 17 by default and use RadPrimer image 10 as the canonical T1 fat-suppressed MR copy.

GENERATOR NOTES
- Use RadPrimer hierarchy/deck routing exactly as supplied in metadata.json.
- Use source labels in later prose when a detail is source-specific.
- Use clean image labels such as RadPrimer image 5 or STATdx image 4 in narrative-facing text; keep short IDs only in traceability metadata.
- Download only selectedPrimaryImageIds by default using sourceSelectionPlan.imageDownloadPlan.
- Do not generate cards or a lecture from this package yet.

RadPrimer.role: Canonical hierarchy/backbone and base Hemorrhagic Cyst article.
keptText: definition of hemorrhage into an ovarian cystic space, most often hemorrhagic corpus luteum
core ultrasound signs: lace-like fibrin strands, retracting avascular clot, posterior enhancement, and claw sign
need to assess pelvic and upper-abdominal hemoperitoneum after rupture
CT/MR overview including high-attenuation blood, fluid-fluid level, and T1 fat-suppressed blood products
differential against endometrioma, solid ovarian mass, torsion, ectopic pregnancy, and pelvic abscess
natural history and SRU management thresholds
limitations: Fewer STATdx-style modality variants and less detail on MR signal variability.
Only one RadPrimer image is exactly duplicated in STATdx; RadPrimer images should remain canonical primary images.

STATdx.role: Supplemental depth and expanded image-recognition set.
keptText: four classic US appearances based on blood-product age
CT detail for sentinel clot sign, ruptured collapsed cyst, wall defect, and high-attenuation hemoperitoneum
MR signal variability by hematocrit, protein concentration, hemoglobin form, and clot formation/retraction
differential additions including dermoid cyst, tuboovarian abscess, and ovarian cancer
same-patient MR/US clusters and additional fishnet, retracting-clot, rupture, and ring-of-fire examples
limitations: STATdx breadcrumb is not used for canonical hierarchy because RadPrimer is present.
STATdx image 17 duplicates RadPrimer image 10 and is archived by default.

radprimerImageCoverageGate.summary: STATdx does not fully cover the RadPrimer image set. It exactly duplicates only RadPrimer image 10; several other RadPrimer images have near or conceptual STATdx reinforcement, and RadPrimer images 4, 6, and 7 are not covered.

coverage.evidence: STATdx contains visually similar reticular/fishnet hemorrhagic cyst examples, but actual evidence images show different screenshots/patients and no shared stable image ID.
STATdx has avascular Doppler hemorrhagic cyst examples, but visual review shows different images; RadPrimer uniquely includes the claw-sign/parenchymal-flow and venous-waveform teaching combination.
STATdx includes pelvic hemoperitoneum from ruptured HOC, but the staged images are visibly different and do not duplicate the RadPrimer cul-de-sac fluid image.
RadPrimer surgical/laparoscopy correlation is not represented in STATdx image evidence.
STATdx image 6 teaches the same ring-of-fire/hemorrhagic corpus luteum pitfall, but the visual evidence is a different Doppler image and source ID.
The bilateral enlarged/kissing ovaries example after stopping birth control is not covered by STATdx image evidence.
STATdx discusses hemoperitoneum but does not provide an upper-abdominal/hepatorenal fossa ultrasound image matching this RadPrimer teaching point.
STATdx CT images show ruptured hemorrhagic cyst with high-attenuation pelvic fluid/sentinel clot, but not the same upper-abdominal axial CT image.
STATdx provides CT rupture cases, but none duplicate the RadPrimer coronal CT showing active bleeding and large upper-abdominal hemoperitoneum.
Actual image_evidence review shows the same axial T1 fat-suppressed MR screenshot/content in RadPrimer image 10 and STATdx image 17, with only source/resolution/crop differences.
